headline: Sequence, reaction and ontology priors are tested for predicting enzyme and metabolite function
label: Sequence Based Enzyme Function Prediction
summary: New benchmarks and priors for enzyme activity, EC assignment and metabolite properties make comparisons of knowledge-informed models possible.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of structured biological knowledge and curated benchmarks to predict function from molecular sequence or structure. Ontology pre-training embeds bio-ontology hierarchy into deep learning to improve metabolite property prediction. A systematic review benchmarks EC number prediction from reaction chemical structures, comparing similarity-based and ML/deep approaches. MCDBench supplies 792 medium-chain dehydrogenase enzyme-substrate-cofactor combinations, including validated inactives, for evaluating predictors. CarmnaDD predicts nitrogenase activity from sequence alone using learnable dual-descriptor weights. A lightweight CNN separating coding from intergenomic DNA (91.87% validation accuracy) is a looser fit, sharing the sequence-model approach but not the enzyme or drug-discovery focus. What is new is the emphasis on negative-inclusive benchmarks and prior-knowledge integration; the items are not evaluated against one another.
